text: With scope locked, this is the first real architecture decision: which tools actually move and process Pinehurst's data, and why the pipeline splits in two.

Pinehurst's point-of-sale vendor only produces one nightly export file per store. An Azure Data Factory pipeline, pl_copy_pos_exports, moves those files from the on-prem file share into Blob Storage -- the one stage that genuinely has to wait on a clock.

Everything after that is continuous, not scheduled: Snowpipe auto-ingests new files, a Stream tracks what changed, and a Task merges just those changes into the clean table, before dbt, via Airflow, builds the Gold models.
We rejected a second nightly batch job and a cron-polling script -- both reintroduce the same scheduled-window problem Snowpipe, Streams, and Tasks were built to remove.
Next: the pipeline moves from the whiteboard into real implementation.
